contract: The road user is motionless at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a sampled reading at or below it is read as no movement at all. The definition this contract carries requires a “complete cessation from movement”, and because speed is sampled and measured with error, the tolerance is the bound within which a reading is read as that cessation; it is the contract's own magnitude and never a figure. The concept states the motion state at the observation and nothing else. Not a stand-in for: a halt of any duration or a halt repeated over a window, a vehicle standing, parked or waiting, the engine being off or a brake being applied, or a halt at a place a law names — it carries no place, no duration and no control state.

params.name: speed_tolerance
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled reading of the road user's speed is read as a complete cessation from movement; it names the source's resolution for a standing body

elements.span: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance
elements.justification: kin.speed is the “magnitude of velocity” of a road user, in m/s, which is exactly the quantity the definition's “complete cessation from movement” bounds. The atom carries no exclusion bearing on this reading; kin.velocity is not read, because the definition speaks of movement and not of its direction.

residues.why: The definition's scope clause tells which of the two posted definitions of the word applies to a given law — the one for a stop that is required rather than prohibited. It is a rule of application, not a condition of the scene, and no observation decides it.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car has braked to rest at a junction: its speed reads zero over several consecutive observations, below the tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car rolls through the same junction at about 2 m/s without stopping: its speed is well above the tolerance at every observation.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with the source declaring the speed of road users absent: no observation decides whether the car was motionless.

contract: The road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that coming to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has begun, and not the state of lying inside the region afterwards. It states no direction of entry, no carrier the road user came through, no speed and no place within the region. Not a stand-in for: lying within the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still inside; the carrier or the way the road user came from, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or a leaving of the region.

elements.span: comes to overlap a structure region at the observation
elements.justification: rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is exactly the overlap of the footprint with the region argument at the observation; the kind of the region is the caller's, since the formal is a region variable the caller binds.

elements.span: did not overlap it at the observation before
elements.justification: the same relation read at the previous observation, which the formula language's 'rises' construct ('phi here and not at the previous observation') states over it; no other atom is read, so the event is the rise of that occupancy and nothing else.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint is clear of the junction polygon at one scene and overlaps it at the next: the concept is true at that next scene.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at both scenes: it is already inside, so the concept is false at the later scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not report whether the car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at the earlier scene, so whether the overlap has just begun is unknown.

contract: The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. The region's direction is read normalised, as its atom states, so the value is a speed along that direction. The quantity is geometric only: it does not state that the road user is on the region, that the region is the one a law names, or how far the road user is from it, and a caller states those with its own relations. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. Not a stand-in for: the direction the body points, which a road user may hold while moving another way, the road user's speed, which is unsigned, or an angle between the two directions.

elements.span: a road user's velocity
elements.justification: kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” of a road user, in m/s in the world frame, whose components are what this quantity projects; kin.speed is not read, being the unsigned magnitude, and kin.heading is excluded because the contract reads the direction of the motion and not the direction the body points.

elements.span: the designated direction of travel of a structure region
elements.justification: st.lane_direction is the “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder”, which “a formula reads … normalised”, exactly as this contract reads it, and whose contract also states that “a centre turn lane carries none” and “a place no carrier covers has none (unknown)”, which the contract's unknown clause carries.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car travels at 8 m/s along a one-way roadway whose designated direction runs the same way: the quantity reads about plus 8 m/s, within bounds the caller sets for travel with the designation.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car travels at 8 m/s the other way along that roadway: the quantity reads about minus 8 m/s, outside those bounds.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same roadway with the source declaring the designated direction of travel of structures absent: the quantity has no direction to project onto and is unknown.

narrowings.span: The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region
narrowings.why: Written as the planar scalar projection vx·dx + vy·dy over the two world-frame components the vector atoms expose (`kin_velocity`, `st_lane_direction`, each read with a component literal), the direction being the normalised one its atom states. The contract names a component along a direction without saying how it is formed; this is the only reading the available atoms allow, and it leaves the height out because the world is planar.

contract: The road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that ceasing to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has ended, and not the state of lying outside the region at the later observations. It states no direction of departure, no carrier the road user leaves through, no speed and no place outside the region. Not a stand-in for: lying outside the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still outside; the carrier or the way the road user goes on to, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or an entry into the region, which has its own concept.

elements.span: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before
elements.justification: rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is the overlap the contract reads at the observation and at the one before; the region is the formal r the caller binds, so no region of the scene other than the one the caller singles out is read. Exclusion: the relation carries the footprint's overlap and not the geometry of the region (st.region_geometry), no distance being read, and not a direction or a speed of departure, which the contract expressly does not state.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle's footprint overlaps an intersection region at one observation and, at the next, lies wholly clear of it: the concept holds at that next observation.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle's footprint overlaps the intersection region at both observations, having only moved farther into it: the concept fails. It fails as well at the observation after the departure, when the footprint lay clear of the region at the observation before.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe which regions the vehicle's footprint overlaps, so whether the overlap with the region has just ended cannot be told.

differs_from.why: The sorts and the atom are the same as drv.motion.region_entry's, but the event is the opposite one: region_entry rises where the footprint comes to overlap the region, having not overlapped it at the observation before, while this concept rises where it ceases to overlap the region, having overlapped it at the observation before. Neither implies the other and no instantiation of one gives the other's verdict.

contract: The road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation is at least the heading change tolerance, a size the caller sets at the resolution of the source. It is a state the road user is in at each observation of a bending path, in either hand, and it states no direction, no angle reached, no beginning and no place. Not a stand-in for: a completed turn or a manoeuvre recognized from an observed onset — which counts the heading change from that onset and not over a window — a steering input, the curvature of the road, a lane change, or a signal or an intention.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the length of the window behind the observation over which the heading change is accumulated

params.name: heading_change_tolerance
params.meaning: the magnitude of heading change over that window below which the reading is not distinguished from straight running; it names the source's resolution and no size of turn

elements.span: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation
elements.justification: prim.heading_change is “the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sampled too sparsely, or a yaw rate is missing”, whose magnitude is exactly the quantity this contract bounds, and whose window is its own parameter, which this concept exposes. Its inputs are the primitive's own and are not claimed again.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A van swings round the corner of a junction: over the window behind the observation its integrated heading change is about forty degrees, well above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same van reverses straight back along a roadway: its integrated heading change over the window is under a degree, below the tolerance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The corner manoeuvre at the start of the recording, where the window behind the observation is truncated, so the primitive's integration is unknown.

contract: Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. It is a relation of place, direction and spacing at the observation. It says nothing of why the road users travel together, of a common destination or origin, of an organizer, or of their speed: a caller that means a moving file states the motion itself. Not a stand-in for: a chain each of whose consecutive spaces is bounded — the reach is measured from u to each member, so a long file is read through the membership of each road user in turn — the class of the members, which the caller states, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.

params.name: min_member_count
params.meaning: the number of road users, u included, at which the group is read as a file rather than as road users happening to follow one another

params.name: file_reach
params.meaning: the distance between the nearest points of two bodies within which another road user is read as travelling with u in the same file

params.name: same_direction_tolerance
params.meaning: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one

elements.span: have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance
elements.justification: rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, the tolerance being the atom's own parameter.

elements.span: lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane
elements.justification: rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is the one-behind-another arrangement this clause states; rel.bearing is not read, giving only a direction and not an in-lane order.

elements.span: are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies
elements.justification: rel.surface_gap is the “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent”, which is the spacing this clause bounds; rel.centre_distance is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Five cars run in file in one lane of a rural highway, each within 20 m of the next and all headings aligned: each of them, counting itself, has at least three members of the group within the reach, ahead of or behind it in the lane.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: One car runs alone in that lane with the nearest other road user 400 m ahead: the minimum member count is not reached within the reach.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The five cars with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: how far apart the members are, and so how many lie within the reach, cannot be read.

narrowings.span: are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies
narrowings.why: The gap is read without a component — the distance between the nearest points of the two bodies — and the bound is inclusive: a road user whose body is exactly the file reach from u's is a member. The contract says `within` without fixing the boundary.

u is counted as a member by identity (`same v u`), not by the three relations holding of u with itself: u is neither ahead of nor behind itself, so the conjunction would exclude it and no file could ever reach its member count. Every other road user is counted only through the relations.

narrowings.span: lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane
narrowings.why: rel.ahead_behind_in_lane states one road user ahead of another along the direction of the lane they share, so the clause is written as that atom in both directions: v ahead of u, or u ahead of v (v behind u).

contract: Road user a is following road user b at the observation: b is ahead of a in the same lane along that lane's direction of travel, and the two bodies' headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a cosine the caller sets. It is a relation of place and direction at the observation; it states no gap, no speed, no duration and no intention. Not a stand-in for: the size of the space between the two — a caller that bounds a space reads the gap atom itself — overtaking or passing, two road users abreast in neighbouring lanes, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.

params.name: same_direction_tolerance
params.meaning: the cosine of the largest angle between the two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one

elements.span: b is ahead of a in the same lane along that lane's direction of travel
elements.justification: rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is exactly the ordering and the frame this contract states; no other atom carries an in-lane order, rel.bearing giving only a direction in the subject's frame.

elements.span: the two bodies' headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance
elements.justification: rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance, which is the cosine of the largest angle allowed, a ratio between -1 and 1”; the tolerance is the atom's own parameter, which this concept exposes as its formal parameter.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car runs in the same lane as a van, 30 m behind it, both headings within a few degrees of each other along the lane.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The car runs abreast of the van in the neighbouring lane: neither is ahead of the other in the same lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same pair with the source declaring the in-lane order of road users absent: whether the van is ahead of the car in its lane cannot be read.

approximations: dismissed: divergence 1 (fails_wrongly) at t=0 ms: Both road users occupy the same eastbound lane, with b ahead of a and their headings identical. At the admissible cosine tolerance 1, their zero heading differe — contract: holds, body: fails; contract: "Road user a is following road user b at the observation: b is ahead of a in the same lane along that lane's direction of" — The verdict turns only on the caller's parameter being set to the degenerate extreme 1, where the atom's strict comparison (cosine "above its tolerance") can never be met; the contract leaves the tolerance to the caller. — "the two bodies' headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a cosine the caller sets"

contract: The road user crosses out of a structure region at the observation: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before, and at the observation it either no longer overlaps that region or overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel which it did not overlap at the observation before. It is the event of that crossing, read at the observation at which it has happened, and not the state of being outside the region afterwards. Not a stand-in for: a turn, since no heading change is read, a signal or a declared intention, a movement that stays within the region however far across it, the completion of a movement into the neighbouring region, or the direction or side the crossing is made towards, which a caller reads from the regions themselves.

elements.span: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before
elements.justification: rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk …)”, which is the occupancy this clause reads, taken at the previous observation by the formula language's own past reading; st.region_geometry is excluded by its own contract, which states that “a footprint inside a boundary is rel.occupies”.

elements.span: overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel
elements.justification: st.lane_adjacency is the “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”, which is the neighbour this clause names, and its exclusion “not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes” does not apply, since the neighbour and not the mark is read; the neighbour is a region of kind st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, which the body's quantifier ranges over, and rel.occupies is the overlap of the footprint with it.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car running in the middle lane of a three-lane carriageway reaches the left-hand lane: at the observation before, its footprint overlapped the middle lane alone; at the observation it overlaps the left-hand lane as well.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car drifts to the left within the middle lane and back again: its footprint overlaps the middle lane and no neighbouring lane at every observation.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same movement with the source declaring the occupancy of regions by road users absent: whether the footprint overlapped the lane before and the neighbour now cannot be read.

narrowings.span: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before
narrowings.why: The language names no past instant of its own; `rises φ` (φ here and not at the observation before) is the only operator that reaches the preceding observation, so the overlap at the observation before is written through it, per branch of the contract's own disjunction: `rises (not occupies r)` where it no longer overlaps the region, and `occupies r and not rises (occupies r)` — overlapping here and not newly so — where it still does.

narrowings.span: overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel
narrowings.why: st.lane_adjacency reads a side (left or right); the contract reads none, since the side the crossing is made towards is excluded, so the body holds the neighbour to be the lane adjacent on either side, disjunctively.

contract: The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached, and it holds at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle, until a later onset starts the count again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a turn begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination. Not a stand-in for: a signal or a declared intention, a steering input, the curvature of the road — a body yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres — a lane change, or a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle and has its own concept.

params.name: heading_step
params.meaning: the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile

params.name: onset_yaw_rate
params.meaning: the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from

params.name: turn_angle
params.meaning: the accumulated heading change at which a turn to the left is recognized

act.onset: the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate
act.recognition: the observation at which that angle is first reached
act.extent: the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle, until a later onset starts the count again
act.history: Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a turn begun before the recording is never read as one made within it.

elements.span: its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)”, in deg/s, which is the quantity whose rise marks the onset; its exclusion “not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres” does not apply, because the body's yaw and not the road's bend is what the contract reads.

elements.span: the heading change accumulated since that onset
elements.justification: The accumulated heading change since an observed onset is integrated from the same atom by the formula language's own construct, which the ontology describes as “the signed heading change of a road user since a formula last became true, integrated from kin.yaw_rate with a step bound”; prim.heading_change is expressly “not a stand-in for it”, being taken over a fixed window behind each observation rather than from an onset, which is why this concept reads the atom and not that primitive.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car running straight begins to swing left: its yaw rate rises above the onset rate, and a second and a half later the heading change accumulated since that observation passes the turn angle.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car changes lane to the left: its yaw rate rises above the onset rate briefly, but the accumulated heading change peaks at a few degrees and never reaches the turn angle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car is already turning at the first observation of the recording, so no onset is observed with the yaw rate known at every observation since: the accumulated change cannot be counted.

narrowings.span: the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate
narrowings.why: The onset is read as the latest observation at which `kin.yaw_rate` of the road user rose definitely above the onset yaw rate (false at the observation before, true there), not the first such rise of the recording: the contract's own words "until a later onset starts the count again" make the count restart at every later onset, so "first rose" is read relative to the judged observation.

contract: Road user a is passing road user b at the observation: the two headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a's speed exceeds b's by at least the speed excess the caller sets, and either the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap — a is drawing level with b — or b is still ahead of a in the same lane. It is the state of a passing manoeuvre at the observation and states no lane used, no clearance between the bodies, no completion of the pass and no right to make it. Not a stand-in for: a completed pass, the lane or side the pass is made on, a signal or an intention, or the clearance between the bodies, which the gap atom carries.

params.name: same_direction_tolerance
params.meaning: the cosine of the largest angle between the two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one

params.name: min_speed_excess
params.meaning: the amount by which a's speed must exceed b's for the two to be read as passing rather than keeping station; it names the resolution of a speed difference

elements.span: the two headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance
elements.justification: rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, with the tolerance the atom's own parameter.

elements.span: a's speed exceeds b's by at least the speed excess
elements.justification: kin.speed is the “magnitude of velocity” in m/s of each road user, so the difference of the two readings is the excess this clause bounds; kin.accel_longitudinal is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for speed”.

elements.span: the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap is “the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections; a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies”, which is the drawing level this clause states.

elements.span: b is still ahead of a in the same lane
elements.justification: rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which carries the earlier part of a pass, before the bodies draw level.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A lorry at 24 m/s draws level with a lorry at 20 m/s on a two-lane highway, their headings aligned and their bodies' projections on the overtaking lorry's heading sharing several metres.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The two lorries run in file at the same speed, 40 m apart: there is no speed excess, so neither is passing the other.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same pair drawing level with the source declaring the speed of road users absent: whether one is gaining on the other cannot be read.

differs_from.why: The two take the same sorts — two road users — but read different atoms and decide differently for the same motion: following reads only the in-lane order and the heading agreement, and is true of a pair that keeps station indefinitely, while passing adds the speed excess and the longitudinal overlap of the bodies and is false of such a pair.

narrowings.span: the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap
narrowings.why: read as a strictly positive shared length of the two projections: the atom is signed, zero where the projections abut and negative for the gap between them, and projections that merely touch at a point are no overlap, so the bound is strict rather than at-or-above zero.

approximations: The disclosed reading of projection overlap as strictly positive shared length, excluding projections that merely touch, is permitted by the contract's wording and is not a demonstrated divergence.

contract: The road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre — the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle, a size the caller sets below a half turn, while the road user's footprint overlaps a way. The definition this contract carries is the turning of a vehicle upon a highway “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”, so halts, rearward movements and steering the other way between the onset and the reversal do not end the manoeuvre, and the count runs on until the angle is reached or a later onset starts it again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached, and it holds at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle, until a later onset starts the count again. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a reversal begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. The reversal angle is the contract's own magnitude, the bound within which a sampled heading change is read as the opposite direction. Not a stand-in for: a turn through a smaller angle, which has its own concept, a turn into another way, travel against a designated direction of travel, a reversing movement, or a signal or a declared intention.

params.name: heading_step
params.meaning: the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile

params.name: onset_yaw_rate
params.meaning: the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from

params.name: reversal_angle
params.meaning: the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized; it is set below a half turn so that a reversal sampled coarsely or made on a skewed way is still recognized

act.onset: the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate
act.recognition: the observation at which that angle is first reached
act.extent: the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle, until a later onset starts the count again
act.history: Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a reversal begun before the recording is never read as one made within it.

elements.span: the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)”, in deg/s, whose magnitude is read here so that a reversal to either hand is recognized; its exclusion of road curvature does not apply, the body's yaw being what is read.

elements.span: the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset
elements.justification: The accumulated heading change since an observed onset is integrated from the same atom by the formula language's own construct, “the signed heading change of a road user since a formula last became true, integrated from kin.yaw_rate with a step bound”; prim.heading_change is expressly “not a stand-in for it”, being taken over a fixed window, which a manoeuvre made “not … by one continuous movement” would fall outside.

elements.span: while the road user's footprint overlaps a way
elements.justification: The definition places the turning “upon a highway”: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic”, and rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, anchors it to the road user, so the concept reads the way the body is on and not any way of the scene.

residues.why: Which devices count as a vehicle is the aggregate the caller states of the road user it passes; the concept is written for any road user and adds no class of its own.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car on a city street swings left across the way, halts to let a vehicle pass, reverses a metre and completes the swing: from the onset of the turning the accumulated heading change reaches about a hundred and seventy degrees while its footprint overlaps the way.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car turns left into a side street: the accumulated heading change since the onset peaks at about ninety degrees and never reaches the reversal angle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car is already mid-turn at the first observation of the recording, so no onset is observed with the yaw rate known at every observation since: whether the direction reversed cannot be read.

differs_from.why: Both take one road user and read the same atom, but they recognize different manoeuvres and decide differently for the same motion: the left turn is recognized at a smaller angle to the left alone, while this concept reads the magnitude of the accumulated change, so it holds for a reversal to either hand and is false of an ordinary junction turn that the left-turn concept recognizes.

narrowings.span: the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate
narrowings.why: The count is anchored to the latest observation at which that magnitude rose above the onset yaw rate (false at the observation before, true there), not to the first such rise of the recording: the contract's own extent fixes this, since "the count runs on until the angle is reached or a later onset starts it again". "First" is therefore read as the first rise of the run the count belongs to.

narrowings.span: while the road user's footprint overlaps a way
narrowings.why: Read at the observation the concept speaks about — the one at which the angle is reached, and each later one at which the accumulated change still holds it — and not as a condition required at every observation from the onset onwards; the contract makes the overlap a circumstance of the reversal it recognizes, not a further bound on the manoeuvre's course.

approximations: The onset-boundary test agreed with the contract: at the observed onset itself, the body fails rather than counting heading change from the preceding interval.
A test with a sampling gap before a fresh onset was dropped because the harness rejected its heading_since history as too sparsely sampled; it established no evaluable divergence.

contract: The road user is travelling rearward at the observation: the component of its velocity along the direction its body points is at most the negative of the reverse speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a rearward component smaller than it is read as none. The concept states the direction of the body's motion relative to the direction it points, at the observation only, and says nothing of how long the rearward motion lasts or where it happens. The whole of it is read from the road user's own velocity and the direction its body points, so no structure region, no device and no control state enters it. Not a stand-in for: the gear selected — a body in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade and one in reverse stands still — a reversing lamp or any other signal, a halt, a turn, the place the motion happens at, or the component of the velocity along a structure region's designated direction of travel, which is a separate quantity read from the region and says nothing of the direction the body points.

params.name: reverse_speed_tolerance
params.meaning: the magnitude of the rearward velocity component below which the motion is not distinguished from a standing body's measurement noise; it names the source's resolution

elements.span: the component of its velocity along the direction its body points
elements.justification: kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” in m/s in the world frame and kin.heading the “direction the body points”, which “a formula reads … normalised”, so the product of the two along the heading is the signed speed in the direction the body points. The ontology directs this reading expressly: kin.gear is “not a stand-in for the direction of motion — a vehicle in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade; backing is read from kinematics”. kin.speed is not read, being unsigned. No region direction is read: st.lane_direction is the “direction of travel designated for a structure”, and the accepted quantity drv.position.direction_component is the component “along the designated direction of travel of a structure region”, which is “not a stand-in for the direction the body points, which a road user may hold while moving another way” — the reference here is the body's own heading, so neither that atom nor that concept belongs to this element and this record's files name neither.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car reverses out of a parking bay at about 1.5 m/s: its velocity points opposite to its heading, so the component along the heading is about minus 1.5 m/s.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car drives forward out of the bay at 1.5 m/s: the component along its heading is about plus 1.5 m/s.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same manoeuvre with the source declaring road-user velocity absent: the direction of the motion relative to the body cannot be read.
